issues.body: crate_labels_to_provision still derives manifests from bare path strings, while fetch_changed_files deliberately discards each REST entry's status and combines filename with previous_filename. Consequently, crates/<name>/Cargo.toml can qualify when it was deleted or is only the source of a rename away. An added file at that path also qualifies without being a valid Cargo manifest or identifying a crate consistent with <name>. This contradicts the load-bearing claim that the PR establishes the crate and can create permanent area-label state for a nonexistent crate. The added tests do not cover any of these cases.
issues.fix_hint: Preserve structured changed-file records including status and distinguish current filename from previous_filename for provisioning. Accept only an added manifest or the destination of a rename at crates/<name>/Cargo.toml. Fetch that PR-head blob as inert data, parse it without executing PR code, and verify that it is a valid package/workspace crate manifest whose identity is consistent with the directory. Add tests proving deletions and rename-away sources never provision, malformed or identity-mismatched manifests never provision, and a valid newly added manifest does.
issues.title: Manifest-path evidence still accepts deleted, renamed-away, or invalid manifests

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant. The round-4 major finding remains: provisioning still treats a bare normalized path equal to crates/<name>/Cargo.toml as proof that a crate exists. fetch_changed_files discards REST status and merges filename with previous_filename into one path list, so a deleted manifest or the old side of a rename can qualify. It also never validates the PR-head manifest as inert data, so malformed content or a package identity inconsistent with the directory can create durable repository label state. The new tests still cover only path shapes and do not exercise deletion, rename-away, malformed manifests, or identity mismatch.
